claim: Overfitting often arises when a model is excessively complex relative to the size and diversity of its training data.
reason: It identifies excessive model complexity relative to the training data as a contributing factor.

claim: Overfitting can occur when the training data is imbalanced, with some classes overrepresented and others underrepresented.
reason: It identifies imbalanced training data as a condition under which overfitting can occur.

claim: Without regularization, models are free to fit training data too closely, increasing the risk of overfitting.
reason: It identifies lack of regularization as a contributing factor and explains how it can increase overfitting.

claim: Training a model for too many epochs can lead to overfitting.
reason: It identifies training for too many epochs as a contributing factor.

claim: Too many features can potentially magnify noise and result in overfitting.
reason: It identifies having too many features as a contributing factor and describes how they can magnify noise.
